statement: Domaine de Saint Pierre is the Mathenay, Jura estate associated with Fabrice Dodane. Dodane joined as manager in 1989 and later acquired/took control of the estate; specialist sources differ between 2011 and 2012 for the transfer, so CARTA does not force an exact takeover year.
Ecocert currently lists Fabrice Dodane / Domaine de Saint-Pierre in Mathenay under EU organic agriculture certification.
INAO describes Arbois as an AOP for still white, red and rosé wines produced in the Jura and links the current legal specification and delimitation resources.

scope_notes: Durable wine identity; composition and cellar details remain vintage-scoped.
statement: Château Renard is a recurring white Arbois bottling of Domaine de Saint Pierre / Fabrice Dodane. Available vintage records show that its detailed composition should be temporalized rather than treated as permanently 100% Chardonnay.
Beaune Imports identifies the 2018 Château Renard as Arbois Chardonnay from Domaine de Saint Pierre / Fabrice Dodane.
iDealwine describes the 2020 Château Renard as Chardonnay complemented by a small proportion of Savagnin. CARTA preserves this as a vintage-specific market-source claim rather than universalizing it.

The Bournet-Lapostolle family developed the Clos Apalta estate/project in Chile beginning with Alexandra Marnier Lapostolle's 1994 Apalta venture; Clos Apalta is also used as the name of the flagship wine, which CARTA models separately from the estate/project.

Clos Apalta identifies Charles-Henri de Bournet Marnier Lapostolle as President and CEO since 2013, Andrea Leon as Technical Director, and Michel Rolland as a consultant personally involved since 1997.

Clos Apalta describes a 60-hectare amphitheatrical vineyard at the entrance of Apalta Valley, mostly southeast-facing, with old vines, granite-derived soils and parcels between 150 and 300 metres; these are estate/vineyard-wide descriptors, not Le Petit Clos parcel geometry.

Clos Apalta states that it has been certified organic since 2009 and currently farms its 60 hectares organically; it describes biodynamic experience without requiring CARTA to infer a separate biodynamic certification.

Le Petit Clos is a recurring named wine in the Clos Apalta portfolio and is modeled as its own durable wine identity, distinct from both the Clos Apalta estate/project and the flagship Clos Apalta wine.
Clos Apalta lists the 2020 Le Petit Clos blend as 40% Carmenère, 38% Cabernet Sauvignon, 19% Merlot and 3% Petit Verdot; the vintage is labeled Appellation Apalta.
Clos Apalta lists the 2021 Le Petit Clos blend as 68% Carmenère, 16% Cabernet Sauvignon, 15% Merlot and 1% Cabernet Franc; the vintage is labeled Appellation Apalta.
Clos Apalta lists the 2022 Le Petit Clos blend as 59% Carmenère, 33% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot and 3% Cabernet Franc and explicitly labels it D.O. Apalta.
Chile's Decree 56, published 25 May 2018, adds Apalta as a viticultural Area within Valle de Colchagua; its boundary is defined by the rural locality of Apalta in the commune of Santa Cruz.
Bodegas Muga is a family winery founded in 1932 by Isaac Muga and Aurora Caño and located in Barrio de la Estación, Haro, within the Rioja Alta wine world.

scope_notes: Durable wine identity across vintages; vintage blend and aging details remain temporal.
statement: Bodegas Muga produces the recurring wine Prado Enea Gran Reserva; the current first-party page presents the 2019 vintage under that durable named identity.
Muga lists Prado Enea Gran Reserva 2019 as Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta and Mazuelo, from high-elevation parcels in the northwest of Rioja Alta around Sajazarra, Cellorigo and Fonzaleche.
For Prado Enea Gran Reserva 2019, Muga documents oak-vat fermentation, at least 36 months in oak, fresh-egg-white clarification before bottling, and at least 36 months of bottle aging.

The current DOCa Rioja Gran Reserva rule for red wine requires five years of total aging, including at least two years in 225-litre oak barrels and two years in bottle; the remaining year can be allocated flexibly.
The Consejo Regulador DOCa Rioja lists Mazuelo with the synonyms Carignan, Cariñena, Mazuela and Samsó.

scope_notes: Informal community of practice / historical cluster, not a formal organization and not proof of bilateral collaboration among every member.
statement: Kermit Lynch identifies Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Jean-Paul Thévenet as Beaujolais/Morgon producers who followed Jules Chauvet's methods and whom Lynch dubbed the 'Gang of Four'; his account credits their adoption of those methods with a dramatic change in Beaujolais wine quality and increased attention to the region.
